# Docker Model Runner — facts

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Practical guidance: choose DMR for Docker-native workflows, OCI artifact distribution and CI (Testcontainers); choose Ollama for rapid prototyping, framework independence and a larger one-command model library. Some CUDA images reportedly hardcode a 4096-token context limit that overrides higher settings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://glukhov.org/llm-hosting/comparisons/docker-model-runner-vs-ollama-comparison/ · keywords: Docker Model Runner

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A single-hardware benchmark (M1 Pro, 50 runs each, model unnamed, March 2025) found DMR 24.53 vs Ollama 23.65 mean tokens/sec, a 0-12% per-prompt difference; the author calls them comparable. Variance was high and the setup was one machine. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-03) — https://connect.hyland.com/t5/alfresco-blog/comparing-llm-runtimes-for-alfresco-in-spring-ai-ollama-vs/ba-p/488667 · keywords: Docker Model Runner · also: https://glukhov.org/llm-hosting/comparisons/docker-model-runner-vs-ollama-comparison/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] DMR supports three inference engines: llama.cpp (default, GGUF, all platforms), vLLM (Safetensors, NVIDIA GPUs; Linux x86_64 and Windows WSL2) and Diffusers (image generation, NVIDIA on Linux). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner.md · keywords: Docker Model Runner · also: https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-model-runner-integrates-vllm/
- [statement] Models are pulled from Docker Hub, any OCI-compliant registry, or Hugging Face; GGUF and Safetensors files can be packaged as OCI artifacts and published to any registry. (high confidence) — https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner.md · keywords: Docker Model Runner · also: https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-model-runner-integrates-vllm/, https://glukhov.org/llm-hosting/comparisons/docker-model-runner-vs-ollama-comparison/
- [statement] DMR serves an OpenAI-compatible API and an Ollama-compatible API. The default local endpoint is http://localhost:12434/v1/chat/completions. (high confidence) — https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner.md · keywords: Docker Model Runner · also: https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-model-runner-integrates-vllm/
- [statement] Engine routing is automatic by model format: a GGUF model uses llama.cpp, a Safetensors model uses vLLM. The vLLM backend is installed once with 'docker model install-runner --backend vllm --gpu cuda'. (medium confidence) — https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-model-runner-integrates-vllm/ · keywords: Docker Model Runner · also: https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner.md
- [statement] Docker announced the vLLM integration on 2025-11-20. At launch it supported only x86_64 with NVIDIA GPUs, had slower startup than llama.cpp, and few vLLM-format models on Docker Hub. Docker recommends prototyping on llama.cpp and scaling to vLLM. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-20) — https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-model-runner-integrates-vllm/ · keywords: Docker Model Runner · also: https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner.md
- [statement] Platform support: macOS needs Apple Silicon; Windows amd64 needs NVIDIA drivers 576.57+ (arm64 uses OpenCL on Adreno); Linux (Docker Engine only) supports CPU, CUDA, ROCm and Vulkan. On macOS/Windows the engines run in a host sandbox, on Linux in a container. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner.md · keywords: Docker Model Runner · also: https://glukhov.org/llm-hosting/comparisons/docker-model-runner-vs-ollama-comparison/
- [statement] The Model Runner API has no authentication: any client that can reach it can pull, load and run models. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.docker.com/ai/model-runner.md · keywords: Docker Model Runner
